title: fix(cli,types): say what `objectui check` does; name `objectui validate` for the verdict (objectui#10524)
body:
Fixes #10524
Clause-②: no

Wording only, on published text: a help string in `@object-ui/cli` and six comments in five `@object-ui/types` files. No export, type, schema or accept set moves. `check` itself is unchanged: objectui#6318 recorded its behaviour as deliberate, and whether it should parse the files it admits is that card's open question, not this one.

The house wording is the one PR objectui#10523 used for the two docs pages: `check` sweeps a project's JSON files and recognises a file whose root carries a structural key (`children`, `className`, `body`, …) by that key alone, without parsing it against the schema (it is still read as JSON). Only a file with none of those keys is parsed against the schema. It is listed by name when its root `type` names a registered component but the document does not validate, and that list is advisory: `check` exits non-zero on unreadable JSON only. The verdict is `objectui validate`'s.

## What changed

| file | change |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/cli/src/cli.ts` | H1. The `check` command's description changes from "Validate schema files" to "Advisory JSON file sweep; run objectui validate for a verdict" (61 characters; the longest sibling description has 57). The line count does not change. |
| `packages/types/src/complex.ts` | H2. In the `ChatbotSchema.body` tombstone docblock, the root-parse parenthetical now names only `objectui validate`. A new sentence says `check` does not deliver the refusal: `body` is a structural root key, and `check` never parses a file it recognised that way against the schema. One line changed and three added. `body?: never` and every other line are byte-identical. |
| `packages/types/src/layout.ts` | H3 hit. The `SemanticElementSchema` docblock said the document "was refused by `objectui check`". It now says `objectui validate`, whose refusal it was. One word changed. |
| `packages/types/src/zod/layout.zod.ts` | H3 hit. The same sentence in the zod mirror's docblock ("REFUSED by `objectui check` … stop trusting the validator") now names `objectui validate`. One word changed. |
| `packages/cli/src/__tests__/cli-bin.test.ts` | H5 pin, 2 cases. `check --help` must not lead with the verb "validate", and it must name `objectui validate`. Both are red on the base and green at the head (evidence below). |
| `packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts` | Rework-round hits (contract review, comment 5831281522). The `ObjectGanttSchema.gantt` comment ("reaches the CLI's `validate`/`check` … refused at authoring time") and the `ObjectCalendarSchema` `sort` comment ("reaches the CLI's `validate` / `check` — `sort: 'name asc'` …") now name `validate` alone. These are `//` comments, and they ship in `dist/zod/objectql.zod.js`. Two lines changed; `git diff -w` shows no code line. |
| `packages/types/src/objectql.ts` | Rework-round hit, the source twin of `.changeset/6475`. The `ObjectGanttSchema.gantt` comment ("therefore the CLI's `validate` / `check` commands") now reads "the CLI's `validate` command". One comment line changed, and it is source-only (a `//` comment on an interface member is dropped from `.d.ts`). The seat decided to fix it here; this seat's other PRs edit this file far from this line. |
| `.changeset/10524-check-promise-text.md` | new: `'@object-ui/cli': patch`, `'@object-ui/types': patch`. The rework rounds tightened it: `check` skips the parse against the schema, not the JSON parse; it names the three objectql comments; and its headline counts six comment sites. |
| 11 pending `.changeset/*.md` | H4 reconciliations, listed below. Front matter md5 is identical before and after for every file. |

## Measurement on the base `6ea68e63e`

The CLI's dependency closure was built with `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter "@object-ui/cli..." build`.

`objectui --help` listed `check                               Validate schema files`, and `objectui check --help` printed `Validate schema files`.

Probe documents, one directory each:

| document | `objectui validate` | `objectui check` over its directory |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{ "type": "chatbot", "messages": [], "body": { "tenant": "acme" } }` | exit 1: `REFUSED (objectui#8572, ADR-0049)`, `Path: body` | exit 0. The file is not mentioned, and the run ends with `✓ All checks passed`. |
| `{ "type": "chatbot", "messages": "not-an-array" }` (control, no structural key) | exit 1 | exit 0. The file is listed as `carries a registered ObjectUI component type but did not validate`. |

So the card's premise holds at the base. `check` admits `chatbot-body.json` by its `body` key and never parses it against the schema. In `check`'s own output, `objectui validate FILE` stands for the angle-bracket placeholder the CLI prints, because GitHub's body sanitizer deletes that shape.

## H5: the pin is red on the base and green at the head

I committed the fix first (`dbbd2506e`). For the base leg, `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (from the objectstack checkout, in wrap mode, with a `trap … EXIT INT TERM` restore as a second guard) put the base description back into `cli.ts`. It reported anchor `x1 -> x0`, replacement `x0 -> x1` and blob `3b73365ae916 -> 165ca5b82c62`. Then the leg rebuilt `@object-ui/cli` and grepped `dist/cli.js`: new text 0 hits, base text 1 hit.

- Base leg: `Tests  2 failed | 38 passed (40)`. The failures were `expected 'Validate schema files' not to match /^\s*validates?\b/i` and `expected 'Validate schema files' to contain 'objectui validate'`.
- Restore: the blob equals HEAD's `3b73365ae916` and `git diff HEAD` is empty. After a rebuild, `dist/cli.js` has 1 hit for the new text and 0 for the base text.
- Head leg: `Test Files  1 passed (1)`, `Tests  40 passed (40)`, and both `check --help does not present ... (objectui#10524)` cases pass. `git status --porcelain` shows 0 lines.

The JSDoc edits carry no pin. They are comments, and I checked them in the built output instead: `dist/complex.d.ts` has 1 hit for "`objectui check` does not deliver it", `dist/layout.d.ts` has 1 for "refused by `objectui validate`", `dist/zod/layout.zod.d.ts` has 1 for "REFUSED by `objectui validate`", and the two layout files have 0 remaining hits for `objectui check`. After the rework round, `dist/zod/objectql.zod.js` has 0 hits for `validate` / `check` in either spelling. Its positive control, "reaches the CLI's `validate` — `sort: 'name asc'`", has 1 hit.

## H4: pending changesets that name `check`

I read every paragraph in `.changeset/` that names `check`: the literal "objectui check", plus `check` in backticks and mentions wrapped across a line break. The test I applied: does the sentence tell an author that `check` gives a verdict (refuses, fails, delivers the refusal)? A sentence that only says `check` calls `safeValidateSchema` or answers green is true, so it stands.

**Reconciled (11).** Each file now names `objectui validate` for the verdict and gains a `⚠️ **Dated note, 2026-09-25 — … — objectui#10524.**` saying what `check` does. Round 3 tightened every note: `check` "never parses against the schema" a file whose root carries a structural key, because it still reads that file as JSON and fails the run when the JSON is unreadable. Front matter is byte-identical in all 12 changesets this PR touches:

- `10478-filter-condition-value-protocol-rule.md`: "now fails `safeValidateSchema`, `objectui check` and `objectui validate`". Its "answered green" sentence stays true of `check`, and the note says so.
- `6475-gantt-block-face-declared.md`: the heading's "validate/check time" and "the CLI's `validate` and `check` commands … **refused**, naming the missing field".
- `7694-chart-series-chart-type-alias-refusal.md`: "Authors meet it … through the CLI's `objectui check` and `objectui validate` commands". Because this file was touched anyway, its five cross-file `path:line` citations became file names (AGENTS.md #11). The "Before" bullet stands.
- `8466-calendar-color-allday-fields.md`: "refused … through `safeValidateSchema`, the path the CLI's `validate` / `check` take".
- `8499-node-slot-registered-arms.md`: "renders correctly in the browser and is refused by `objectui check`". Its "Downstream" paragraph is about the advisory list and stands.
- `8505-grid-columns-breakpoint-narrowing.md`: "the JSON authoring face — `os-ui validate` / `check` … now refuses `{ xxl: 6 }`". The command's name is also corrected to `objectui validate` in the same clause.
- `8572-chatbot-body-retired.md`: "(`tsc`, `objectui validate`, `objectui check`, …)". This is the changeset twin of the H2 docblock.
- `9239-object-calendar-data-array-arm.md`: "reached by `safeValidateSchema` and so by the CLI's `validate` / `check` … refused AT the key".
- `9511-record-id-is-a-string.md`: its "Delivery surface" paragraph listed `objectui check` on the parse-time side.
- `9559-filter-operator-schema-protocol-set.md`: "(and `objectui check` / `objectui validate`) refused filters".
- `9746-render-path-not-a-validation-door.md` (empty front matter): "the three doors that do validate (…; `objectui validate` / `objectui check`; …)". Here the objectui#10533 "at this change" scoping is used, because the section did say that at that change. The note records the later correction by objectui#10416.

A deviation from H4 as dispatched: for the other ten I did not use "at this change" scoping. Those sentences were never true of `check`, so scoping them would assert a false history. The sentence is corrected instead, and the dated note records the correction.

**Read, and left as they are.** Each of these is either true of `check` or is not a verdict claim:

- `6074`: "judges, skips and prints exactly what it did before".
- `6075`: recognition by validation, and the advisory report.
- `6320`: the glob ignore list.
- `7004`: `.success` used as a boolean recogniser.
- `7113` ("the `chart: 2` entry in `objectui check`'s 28-file census") and `6939` ("`objectui check` counts four for this row"): both are counts of the advisory list. In the filter-builder case, the four leaf fixtures carry no structural key and `search-interface.json` carries `children` and `className`, so the count is right.
- `6051`, `7664`, `8344`: `check` calls `safeValidateSchema`. That is true of the validity arm, and none of these three attributes a refusal to `check`.
- `8516`: `check` "was passing documents `tsc` rejects", which is true.
- `8802` ("will NOT flag either namespaced spelling"), `9641` and `unknown-component-type-case-suggestion-5247`: they describe the unknown-type warning for recognised files.
- `check-schema-positive-marker-and-skip-count`: the marker gate.
- `6724`: `ctx.check` is the permissions API, not the CLI.
- `10393`, `8760`, `9533`: these describe the unknown-type warning, not a validation verdict, so H4 does not cover them. Their bare-document examples are the finding below.

## Other places that make the same promise (H3), swept again in the rework round

The first sweep of package sources used only the literal `objectui check`, so it missed three sentences written as the CLI's `validate`/`check`. The rework sweep ran over `packages/cli` and `packages/types` sources, excluding tests and CHANGELOGs, with three passes:

1. `git grep` for the literal `objectui check`, backticked `check`, `/ check`, `check command(s)` and `'check'`.
2. `git grep` for `check` within 40 characters of `validate`, `CLI` or `refus`.
3. A node scan across line breaks, for `validate` / `check` pairs wrapped over a comment line, and `CLI's … check`.

On the head, pass 3 has 0 hits. Its positive control is the pre-fix blobs of `objectql.zod.ts` and `objectql.ts`, which give 2 and 1 hits. Every hit I read, with its verdict:

| hit | verdict |
| --- | --- |

| `zod/objectql.zod.ts`, the `ObjectCalendarSchema` `sort` comment ("`validate` / `check` — `sort: 'name asc'` … refused at authoring time") | changed: names `validate` alone |
| `objectql.ts`, the `ObjectGanttSchema.gantt` comment ("the CLI's `validate` / `check` commands … refused at authoring time") | changed: names `validate` alone |
| `complex.ts`, the `ChatbotSchema.body` docblock | this PR's own sentence ("`objectui check` does not deliver it") |
| `layout.ts` and `zod/layout.zod.ts`, the `SemanticElementSchema` docblocks | changed in round 1 |
| `data-display.ts` `BarChartSchema` ("`objectui check` reports it as unrecognised") and `zod/data-display.zod.ts` ("could only report it") | stands: describes the advisory list, not a verdict |
| `form.ts` `CodeEditorSchema` ("the validator `objectui validate` and `objectui check` read") | stands: `check` reads `AnyComponentSchema` as its recogniser |
| `strict-authoring-face.ts` (wiring `objectui check` "is ruled to come after") | stands: future wiring, no present claim |
| `zod/complex.zod.ts` (`safeValidateSchema`, `objectui check` and `objectui validate` "answered green") | stands: true of `check`; the file is held by another seat and not touched |
| `packages/cli/README.md`, the heading "`objectui check`, `objectui doctor`, …" | stands: defers to `objectui --help` |
| `packages/cli/src/cli.ts`, `.command('check')` | the command registration; its description is the H1 line |
| `check.ts`: "`objectui check` judged every root `type`", "the reason `check` reports a third bucket", "the `objectui check` command passes", "`objectui check` exited 1 in any TypeScript project" | stand: the marker gate's history, the advisory bucket, the `cwd` parameter, and the JSONC parse arm, all true |
| `known-schema-types.ts` ("`objectui check` uses it", "reports an unrecognised type as a warning and never fails the run") | stands: true |
| `known-type-case-suggestion.ts` ("Did you mean for `objectui check`", "`check` still reports `Page` as an unknown schema type", "the suggestion clause `objectui check` appends") | stands for this card: the unknown-type warning, not a validation verdict. It has the same recognised-files-only boundary as the finding below. It is an internal comment. |
| `union-arm-diagnostics.ts` ("a DIFFERENT surface (`objectui check`)") | stands: names the surface |
| `index.ts` `name:'check'`, `layout.ts` "`check`, `arrow-right`", `zod/layout.zod.ts` `icon:'check'` (four lines) | not the CLI: the lucide glyph name |
| `data-protocol.ts` "PRE-CHECK", `strict-authoring-face.ts` "such a check can only ADD refusals", `zod/complex.zod.ts` "the type check (`id: 42` now refuses)", `zod/objectql.zod.ts` "`.check()` refusing `kanban.groupBy`" and "Until this check" | not the CLI: refinements and value checks |

## Acceptance notes

These are not filed.

- Some test comments still say `check` refuses or validates: the header of `node-slot-registered-arms-8499.test.ts`, one comment in `filter-builder-mirror-6939.test.ts`, and the headers of `filter-condition-value-protocol-rule-10478.test.ts` and `chart-data-model-7113.test.ts`. Tests are not published, and no assertion depends on those comments.
- `7546-chart-series-keys-declared.md` counts `objectui check` among the consumers of the parse output. `check` reads only `.success`, so it loses nothing. That sentence does not claim a verdict.
- `7773-kanban-adapter-groupfield-write.md` names `os check` / `os validate`, which is not this CLI. It was not measured.
- `8516-8556-mirror-partial-record-narrowing.md` spells the CLI as `os-ui validate`, and the bin is `objectui`. Its `check` clause is true.
- In `check.ts`, the inline comment "Schema validation: check for ObjectUI schema patterns" is a code comment that ships in no user-facing output. It is outside this file surface.

## For the seat

- File surface: `layout.ts`, `zod/layout.zod.ts`, `objectql.ts` and `zod/objectql.zod.ts` are H3 hits inside `@object-ui/types`. `objectql.ts` is here by seat decision. Each edit is confined to its comment lines, away from the lines PR #10588 and the objectui#10518 branch edit. `git merge-tree --write-tree` of this head against PR #10588's head `313ca6321` exits 0, and against `claude/issue-10518-object-chart-axis-config` it also exits 0. The claim comment's surface names only the `complex.ts` docblock, so it needs these four paths appended.
- A finding outside this card: `.changeset/8760-unfulfilled-chart-stubs.md` says `{ "type": "line-chart" }` makes `objectui check` report `Unknown schema type "line-chart"`, and `.changeset/9533-dashboard-bare-key-converge-plugin-namespace.md` says the same for `{ "type": "view:dashboard" }`. On the base, `check` over those exact bare documents prints `Skipped 2 files with a root "type" that no ObjectUI recogniser admitted.` and exits 0, with no unknown-type line. The control `{ "type": "line-chart", "className": "h-64" }` prints `⚠️ Unknown schema type "line-chart" in line-chart-structural.json`. `10393-retire-bare-map-key.md`'s "so the check now flags it" has the same boundary. This is a claim about how far a diagnostic reaches, not a verdict claim, so the contract review graded it a different family with its own card; the seat filed it as objectui#10606. That card can reuse PR objectui#10523's recognition-gate wording.
